transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-12 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Ravi Patel, Elena Korovin, Michael Torres, Jasmin Lee (Stormhaven)

--- Summary block (auto-gen, may be rough) ---
Short summary: looked at heatmap, two main regression clusters, decided on bisect + rollback rehearsal, handed off security docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we kept it to 45 minutes today, quick agenda — heatmap review, two regressions, bisect plan, rollback drill, security handoff.
[00:00:15] Ravi Patel: Yep, thanks Maya. Quick ask up front — we had a spike in false positives on the claims route yesterday. Wanted to see root cause.
[00:00:25] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Ravi, we pulled the heatmap just now, you'll see two clusters — cluster A around prompt set #3 expansions, cluster B is more of formatting edgecases from the ingestion normalizer.
[00:00:40] Elena Korovin: Right, cluster B is the one that confused our downstream rules; people were seeing entity hallucinations when the input had trailing metadata.
[00:00:51] Michael Torres: And from security side, are any of these failures leaking PII into logs or external calls? We need to know for SOC2 scope.
[00:01:00] Liam O'Connor: Short answer: we don't see external calls, but the KV "cash" — kv cache — sorry, the KV cache prefix retention could make debugging traces look like they're holding more context. We can scrub logs, and we have a config to zero retention for test endpoints.
[00:01:18] Maya Chen: Quick note — sorry, Liam, KV cash is hilarious, we should keep that.
[00:01:23] [laughter]
[00:01:28] Ravi Patel: Ha. But seriously, can we prioritize cluster A — that's the one that hit production yesterday at 11am and affected 2.3% of requests.
[00:01:38] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, cluster A stems from prompt expansion we shipped last week — we added optional clarifiers to improve precision but the downstream scorer is overweighting some tokens, so you'll see lower BLEU-ish style match on the scoring.
[00:01:52] Elena Korovin: We're using a composite score — token-level match + semantic sim — and the sim model moved our threshold boundary.
[00:02:03] Maya Chen: Can you say more about that threshold movement — is it model drift or just prompt-engine artifact?
[00:02:10] Elena Korovin: Feels like artifact; the new clarifiers change token distributions and the sim embedding picks up paraphrase variance.
[00:02:18] Liam O'Connor: Right, so immediate mitigation options: roll back the prompt expansion, tighten guardrail threshold for sim score, or apply a prompt surgery (we have a small patch that neutralizes the clarifier in edge contexts). Each has cost/impact tradeoffs.
[00:02:33] Jasmin Lee: How long to test the prompt surgery? We can't have a long validation delay.
[00:02:38] Liam O'Connor: We can run A/B in Dedicated sandbox today; full bake is 1-2 business days. But we can do a canary at 10% for 6 hours and watch the scorecard.
[00:02:49] Ravi Patel: I'm nervous about canaries — after yesterday's spike we want a quick rollback plan.
[00:02:55] Maya Chen: That's why we're proposing a rollback drill — rehearsal where we flip traffic to the previous prompt bundle and exercise the detector. It's quick if we pre-stage the rollback playbook.
[00:03:07] Michael Torres: Does rollback require redeploy or is it just a routing rule change? From our compliance view, simpler is better.
[00:03:13] Liam O'Connor: Good Q — it's a routing flag. On Redwood Dedicated/Private it's a config toggle in the runtime control plane, no model deploy required. For hosted customers it's a version pin rollback, which is still under 2 minutes.
[00:03:26] Elena Korovin: Ok, that sounds fine.
[00:03:30] Maya Chen: For the drill we need to agree a window — Ravi suggested morning 2027-10-18 — does that work?
[00:03:36] Ravi Patel: Tentatively yes, morning is best. We'll lock in once we get the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:03:41] Liam O'Connor: On the bisect: we'll take prompt set #4 and run a binary bisection to isolate which added clarifier causes the score drop. We'll attach failing examples. That should find the 3-4 candidate phrases.
[00:03:55] Elena Korovin: Please include our expected labels with the examples; our scorer does some label smoothing so it's helpful.
[00:04:03] Liam O'Connor: Will do.
[00:04:06] Michael Torres: Security handoff — Maya, you mentioned sending SOC2 artifacts.
[00:04:11] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send a security packet — SOC2, ISO attestation, our SSO/SAML guide, and the KMS integration notes. We'll put a link in the doc; here's the placeholder: https://redwood.example/soc2-stormhaven (will replace with real link).
[00:04:25] Michael Torres: Also need info on log retention, PII redaction, and where audit logs live.
[00:04:31] Liam O'Connor: Audit logs live in the control plane; retention configurable per account. We can push a policy that masks any tokens and strips PII within 24 hours; for Private we can integrate with your HSM.
[00:04:44] Maya Chen: We'll add a short checklist to the packet: SSO contact, KMS contact, retention policy, and point-of-contact for audit requests.
[00:04:53] Jasmin Lee: Back to quality — any quick wins to reduce the 2.3% spike before the drill?
[00:04:58] Liam O'Connor: Quick wins: tighten sim threshold by 0.05, reduce max prefix expansion for clarifiers from 3 tokens to 1 token in edge contexts, and enable prefix KV caching so the model sees consistent context. That should cut the false positive rate by about half in our estimate.
[00:05:15] Elena Korovin: The KV caching you mean — be careful, earlier you said KV cash, that's a different repo — but yes we can toggle that.
[00:05:23] [laughs and cross talk]
[00:05:28] Ravi Patel: If we tighten threshold, do we risk recall loss?
[00:05:31] Liam O'Connor: There's a small recall tradeoff — estimated 0.4% absolute. We can mitigate by tuning the scorer weighting temporarily. Also we can whitelist high-confidence routes.
[00:05:43] Maya Chen: For the record, we'll run a quick sim-threshold sweep in the sandbox and send results.
[00:05:49] Liam O'Connor: Also note — quant profile change we tried last month might slightly change decoding entropy; that's separate but worth noting.
[00:05:57] Elena Korovin: We did see small differences after quant switch but that didn't align with this particular regression.
[00:06:05] Jasmin Lee: Any mention of cost impacts? Tightening thresholds or caching — does that increase token costs?
[00:06:12] Maya Chen: Caching reduces per-token cost; tighter sim thresholds don't change cost. The canary and bisect runs will add minimal test load. We'll include token/cost delta in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:06:24] Ravi Patel: Ok, logistics — what artifacts will you send now?
[00:06:28] Maya Chen: We'll send: benchmark sheet, rollback runbook, SOC2 packet link, bisect plan, and a small patch candidate for the prompt surgery.
[00:06:36] Liam O'Connor: We'll also upload the failing cases and the raw scoring logs to the shared bucket; note some transcription noise might show up in the logs.
[00:06:44] Michael Torres: About the shared bucket — is that in your cloud or ours? We need to enforce our retention rules.
[00:06:49] Liam O'Connor: We'll put the test artifacts in a temporary Redwood bucket with 7-day retention and send a signed link. If you'd prefer your bucket, we can push the artifacts there via our service account.
[00:07:02] Ravi Patel: Prefer our bucket — security team will coordinate.
[00:07:06] Michael Torres: I'll send a vendor bucket whitelist.
[00:07:10] Maya Chen: Great.
[00:07:13] [fast forward — heatmap walkthrough, 00:07:13 to 00:20:00 — highlights captured below]
[00:07:13] Liam O'Connor: (screen) Heatmap shows spike on 10/11 11:05-11:35 across claims route. You can see two clusters mapped to prompt set IDs. Cluster A has avg sim score drop from 0.78 to 0.61.
[00:07:35] Elena Korovin: Ok that's a big drop. Any correlation with request length?
[00:07:40] Liam O'Connor: Minimal; distribution looks similar. It's the clarifier token distribution.
[00:07:48] Ravi Patel: We also noticed a couple of examples where trailing JSON in the input caused the scorer to misclassify.
[00:07:54] Liam O'Connor: That's cluster B — formatting edgecases. For that we recommend a small pre-normalizer that strips trailing metadata before scoring.
[00:08:02] Maya Chen: We'll add that to the bisect scope as a quick fix.
[00:08:06] Elena Korovin: Sounds good.
[00:08:10] [discussion of sample failing examples, timestamps omitted]
[00:18:35] Liam O'Connor: Bisect plan: we run binary split over the clarifier set, each run ~1k samples, will produce a ranked list of candidate clarifiers impacting sim. Expect results by EOD 10/15.
[00:18:47] Maya Chen: We'll also stage a small patch for prompt surgery — neutralize clarifier in suffix contexts — if bisect points to that.
[00:18:55] Jasmin Lee: What about guardrails — are you proposing to relax or tighten?
[00:19:00] Liam O'Connor: Tighten sim threshold for the problematic route, keep others same. We can also add a rule to fallback to older prompt bundle if post-score falls below a safety floor. That's part of the rollback playbook.
[00:19:14] Ravi Patel: Good.
[00:19:16] Michael Torres: On the rollback playbook — will you provide a runbook that lists steps, owners, and estimated time-to-recover? We need that for our ops runbook.
[00:19:25] Maya Chen: Yes — owners map to Redwood ops and your on-call. We'll include estimated TTL for rollbacks and an escape hatch to pause traffic.
[00:19:33] Liam O'Connor: Example steps: 1) toggle routing flag, 2) verify scorecard at 5 & 30 minutes, 3) if issues persist, flip traffic back and open incident. Estimated flip time < 2 minutes, verification window 30 minutes.
[00:19:50] Elena Korovin: Will the toggle be auditable?
[00:19:53] Liam O'Connor: Yes, audit logs and timestamped events saved in the control plane. We'll show you the UI in the next demo.
[00:20:02] [discussion about demo scheduling]
[00:20:12] Maya Chen: Alright, quick alignment on deliverables and timing.
[00:20:16] (Items restated)
[00:20:18] Maya Chen: Redwood to send benchmark sheet (10/14), bisect results (10/15), SOC2 packet (10/14), propose rollback drill 10/18.
[00:20:29] Ravi Patel: We'll provide failing prompts (10/14) and confirm drill window (10/15).
[00:20:35] Michael Torres: I'll send the vendor whitelist and SSO contact (10/16).
[00:20:41] Jasmin Lee: Sounds good.
[00:20:45] [closing chatter]
[00:21:00] Maya Chen: One tiny ask — if worst case we can't fix by 10/18, do you want us to just roll back immediately?
[00:21:07] Ravi Patel: Yes, if regression is severe, roll back. We prefer that.
[00:21:12] Maya Chen: Ok noted.
[00:21:15] Liam O'Connor: I'll start the bisect run after this call and share logs.
[00:21:20] Elena Korovin: Thanks.
[00:21:22] Maya Chen: Thank you all. We'll follow up with links and the spreadsheet.
[00:21:27] [meeting end — rest of recording is ambient silence]
